profile.address: Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, Canary Islands, Spain
profile.reading: This data center in Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, in Spains Canary Islands, was originally built by IdecNet, a regional connectivity and data center operator founded in 1995 that ran its own fiber network across Gran Canaria and Tenerife and served more than 1,100 business, public administration, and carrier clients, reporting over 4 million euros in revenue in 2023. Grupo Aire, a mainland Spanish IT services and hosting group, integrated IdecNet into its portfolio in a deal announced January 11, 2024, gaining this Canary Islands data center as part of a strategy the companys leadership described as strengthening its commitment to offering complete, personalized technology solutions and consolidating its presence in the archipelagos telecommunications market. IdecNet held ISO/IEC 27001 information security and Spains ENS, or Esquema Nacional de Seguridad, certifications at the time of the acquisition, standards Grupo Aire has continued operating the facility under following the integration. Grupo Aire itself traces back to 1996, when founders Miguel Tecles, Raul Aledo, and Emilio Gras began their first ServiHosting project together; the company has since grown into a Spanish telecommunications provider offering connectivity, VoIP, MVNO and MVNE wholesale mobile services, unified communications, cloud, and data center services, operating a connectivity network spanning more than 33,000 kilometers across Spain and Portugal and reporting that 40 percent of independent mobile virtual network operators in the Spanish market rely on its infrastructure. Grupo Aire markets this location specifically under the Aire Canarias brand, positioning it as the groups dedicated Canary Islands data center and connectivity hub distinct from its mainland Spanish and Portuguese network sites. Grupo Aire lists the site among its network operations centers supporting continuity for customers across the Canary Islands.
